title: Enable Customers to Reset Their Password
businessObjective: Allow customers to securely reset forgotten passwords, reducing support calls and maintaining account security.
preconditions: Customer has a registered account with a valid email address
Customer is on the login page
Password policy is defined in the system

mainFlow.action: Customer clicks the "Forgot password" link on the login page.
mainFlow.expected: System displays the password reset request form.

mainFlow.action: Customer enters their registered email address and submits the form.
mainFlow.expected: System validates email format and existence, generates a one‑time reset token (expires in 30 minutes), stores it, and sends a reset link to the email.

mainFlow.action: Customer receives the email and clicks the reset link.
mainFlow.expected: System verifies the token is valid and unexpired, then presents the new password entry screen.

mainFlow.action: Customer enters a new password that complies with the password policy and confirms it.
mainFlow.expected: System validates the password and confirmation, updates the customer's password, invalidates the token, signs out all active sessions, and shows a success confirmation message.

alternateFlows.name: Mobile Password Reset Request
steps: Customer accesses the login page via a mobile browser or banking app.
Customer taps the "Forgot password" link, which displays a mobile‑optimized reset request form.
Customer enters email and submits; system behaves identically to the web flow, sending the reset link.

alternateFlows.name: Resend Reset Link
steps: Customer selects "Resend link" on the expired‑link error screen.
System generates a new token, updates the stored token, and sends a fresh reset email.

exceptionFlows.name: Invalid or Non‑existent Email
exceptionFlows.condition: Submitted email does not match any registered account.
exceptionFlows.action: System displays a generic error message: "If the email is registered, a reset link will be sent," without revealing account existence.

exceptionFlows.name: Expired/Used/Invalid Reset Token
exceptionFlows.condition: Customer clicks a reset link that is expired, already used, or malformed.
exceptionFlows.action: System shows an error message: "The reset link is invalid or has expired." and provides a button to request a new reset link.

exceptionFlows.name: Password Policy Violation
exceptionFlows.condition: New password does not meet the defined password policy.
exceptionFlows.action: System highlights the policy requirements and prevents submission until the password complies.

dataRequirements.rules: Must be a valid email format; must exist in Customer table.
Stored hashed; expires after 30 minutes; single‑use.
Minimum 12 characters, at least one uppercase, one lowercase, one digit, one special character; must not match last 5 passwords.

acceptanceCriteria: Given a registered customer is on the login page and selects “Forgot password,” when they enter the email address linked to their account, then the system sends a one-time password-reset link to that email address.

Given the customer opens a valid, unexpired reset link, when they enter a new password that meets the password policy and confirms it, then the system updates the password, signs out all active sessions, and displays a success confirmation

Given the customer uses an expired, already-used, or invalid reset link, when they attempt to reset their password, then the system displays a clear error message and provides an option to request a new reset link
nonFunctionalRequirements: All communications must use TLS 1.2 or higher.
Reset token must be generated using a cryptographically secure random number generator.
Email delivery shall occur within 5 seconds of request under normal load.
The password reset pages must be responsive and pass WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility criteria on both desktop and mobile browsers.
System must log reset requests and token validations for audit purposes, retaining logs for 12 months.
